titre: The Little Prince Was Born in New York
accroche: Written in exile and first published in New York in 1943, The Little Prince did not appear in French, in France, until 1946.
contenu_vulgarise:
A New York apartment, a night in 1942. Antoine de Saint-Exupéry is writing at the table of his friend Silvia Hamilton, a cigarette in his hand, a cup of coffee cooling beside the manuscript. The book he is writing, in French, in a city where he has lived in exile for two years, will become *Le Petit Prince* (*The Little Prince*), one of the most widely read French books in the world. And yet not one of its pages was written in France.

## Published in New York, Not in Paris

Saint-Exupéry fled occupied France for New York in 1940. He writes *Le Petit Prince* in 1942, sometimes in a rented house on the coast of Long Island, sometimes at Silvia Hamilton's, whose black poodle serves as the model for the sheep and a child's doll as the model for the little prince. The manuscript now kept at the Morgan Library, in New York, still bears the marks of this night work: coffee stains, cigarette burns, whole pages crossed out.

The book appeared in April 1943, from the New York publisher Reynal & Hitchcock, in English and in French at the same time, in two nearly identical volumes sold for two dollars each. It is the only time this publisher printed a text by Saint-Exupéry in its original language: the war had cut off access to French presses. The English translation, by Katherine Woods, runs to about 17,000 words, three thousand more than the French original. Saint-Exupéry had never illustrated a book before, however: he draws the watercolors himself, rather than entrusting this work, as usual for his earlier books, to an independent illustrator.

## An Author Who Never Saw His Book Published at Home

Saint-Exupéry has no time to enjoy the book's success. Called back to the colors, he sails for North Africa with a single copy of the freshly printed French edition. On July 31, 1944, he takes off from Corsica on a solitary reconnaissance mission over the south of France. Like the little prince vanished in the desert, he does not return.

Gallimard, the French publisher, brought out its own edition of the book only in 1946, two years after his death: Saint-Exupéry never saw *Le Petit Prince* published in his own country. The manuscript, for its part, stayed for a long time in the hands of Silvia Hamilton, later Reinhardt, before she sold most of it to the Morgan Library in 1968, a quarter of a century after a night of writing at her table, in a Manhattan apartment.

repere.texte: The preparatory manuscript of The Little Prince kept at the Morgan Library runs to 140 pages and 35 full-page drawings; Saint-Exupéry left it, one evening in 1943, in a crumpled paper bag on the table of his friend Silvia Hamilton, before going back to the war.
repere.source: The Morgan Library & Museum, “The Little Prince: A New York Story”

carte.punch: The Little Prince was written and first published in New York, not in Paris.
carte.idee: Saint-Exupéry writes The Little Prince in exile in New York, where the book appears in April 1943, in French and in English. Occupied France would not read it until 1946, two years after the death of its author, who never saw it published at home.

quiz.question: Why can we say that The Little Prince is first of all a New York book?
choix: Because the French publisher Gallimard had moved its presses to New York during the war
Because the book tells the adventures of a New York child disguised as a prince
Because Saint-Exupéry wrote the book after settling permanently in the United States in 1946
Because Saint-Exupéry wrote it and first published it in New York, in exile, before any French edition
quiz.explication: Gallimard did not move its presses: it simply waited until 1946 to publish its own edition. The book is not set in New York, and Saint-Exupéry never settled there after 1943. He wrote and published The Little Prince there in exile, between 1940 and 1943, before going back to fight and disappearing in 1944.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What models does Saint-Exupéry use, at Silvia Hamilton's, to draw the sheep and the little prince of the book?
choix: His friend's black poodle and a child's doll
A Siamese cat and a dressmaker's mannequin
Wooden toys brought back from his childhood
quiz_supplementaire.explication: Silvia Hamilton's black poodle serves as the model for the sheep, and a child's doll serves as the model for the little prince, according to the account kept by the Morgan Library.

quiz_supplementaire.question: Who illustrates The Little Prince, although Saint-Exupéry had never drawn the pictures for a book before?
choix: An independent illustrator hired specially by Reynal & Hitchcock
Saint-Exupéry himself, who draws the watercolors
Silvia Hamilton, at whose home he writes part of the text
Katherine Woods, the book's English translator
quiz_supplementaire.explication: Unlike his earlier books, illustrated by an independent illustrator, Saint-Exupéry draws the watercolors of The Little Prince himself, although he had never illustrated a book before.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What becomes of the manuscript of The Little Prince after Saint-Exupéry's death, before it reaches the Morgan Library?
choix: It is destroyed in a fire at the offices of Reynal & Hitchcock
It immediately joins the Gallimard archives in Paris in 1946
It stays in the hands of Silvia Hamilton, later Reinhardt, until 1968
It is handed over to the French army as part of his military file
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The manuscript stays in the hands of Silvia Hamilton, later Reinhardt, until she sells most of it to the Morgan Library in 1968, a quarter of a century after the night of writing at her table.
